author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader sees every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it named first name then last name. One page, no paging; a veterinarian with no specialty does not appear.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on one page, with no paging
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the directory is opened, then each of them is shown by first name followed by last name
given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each specialty held
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
edge case 1: given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the directory is opened, then the specialty is still listed with no veterinarian under it
edge case 2: given a clinic that knows no specialties, when the directory is opened, then the page renders empty rather than failing
edge case 3: given the same stored data, when the directory is opened twice, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same order
edge case 4: given a specialty name, when the directory is opened, then the name is shown as stored and is not translated
edge case 5: given the directory page, when it is rendered, then it carries the navigation every page carries (REQ-SYS-001) and no navigation entry anywhere points to it
the page's own fixed wording is drawn from the shared wording set in every supported language, with none hard-coded (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the page — read-only view only (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page pointing to the specialty directory — reachable by URL only in this slice; a visible entry point may follow as a separate request
paging, filtering, sorting controls, or search over specialties (NG-9 already excludes veterinarian search)
showing veterinarians who hold no specialty — the page lists specialties, not the roster
notes: Product owner settled two decisions on 2026-08-24 and supplies no further product input: read-only scope, and URL-only reachability. Every other open choice took the narrowest reading and is recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions — listing order (stability is required, the order itself is unstated), whether an unheld specialty carries a marker, and whether a visible entry point follows. Do not design past those; raise a consultation-request if implementation depends on one. Specialty names are data shown as stored; REQ-LANG-002 binds the page chrome only.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely inside the vet feature package (system-design.md § Package Structure). No new module, no new dependency, no schema change, no mapping change. Two facts make it new ground rather than a repeat of the vet list. First, the Vet-Specialty association is unidirectional from Vet, so no query returns specialty-with-veterinarians, and a specialty held by nobody is unreachable through VetRepository.findAll(); a new SpecialtyRepository supplies every stored specialty, on the PetTypeRepository/VetRepository precedent. Second, the page's shape has to be derived, and putting that derivation in a controller would be a fresh Web-controller violation under architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog. It goes in a new immutable value type, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry, with a pure static factory over the two collections. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-24-read-model-derivation-in-value-types.md and in system-design.md § Contracts.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html served by a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package; no request parameter, so no data binder and no id-disallow list is needed (security-principles.md, mass-assignment row)

SpecialtyController injects SpecialtyRepository and the existing VetRepository by constructor, calls SpecialtyDirectoryEntry's static factory, puts one model attribute (suggested name specialtyDirectory) and returns view name vets/specialtyList
SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with a single @Transactional(readOnly = true) Collection<Specialty> findAll(); narrow Repository base like VetRepository, not JpaRepository

Template vets/specialtyList.html uses the shared layout fragment; pass a menu key that matches no nav item (for example 'specialties') so the page carries the navigation without marking any entry active and without adding one
Page chrome reuses the existing bundle keys 'specialties', 'vets' and 'name'; specialty names and veterinarian names render as stored via th:text, never through the message source

patterns.description: declarative Spring Data interface on the narrow Repository base with @Transactional(readOnly = true); SpecialtyRepository copies this shape. Do not add @Cacheable: a new cache name would have to be declared in CacheConfiguration and would inherit the unresolved vet-cache eviction question (system-design.md § Open Questions, item 5)
precedent for a lookup-value repository serving a list; note it orders in the query — this slice deliberately does not, because ordering belongs to the factory where a unit test reaches it
existing name-ordered view over a specialty set; the directory's chosen order follows it — specialties by stored name, veterinarians by last name then first name then id
controller shape to mirror: package-private @Controller, constructor injection, one GetMapping per surface, model attributes then a view-name return
th:each row rendering with escaped th:text and the vet full name composed as firstName + ' ' + lastName; the directory nests a veterinarian loop inside a specialty loop

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets"), so the returned Collection is the cached instance. Sorting it in place corrupts the cache for every later request, including /vets.html
risks.mitigation: the factory treats both inputs as read-only: copy before sorting, and the record stores List.copyOf of its veterinarian list

risks.risk: Ordering split between a repository query and the factory would leave edge case 3 (stable order) only testable against a database
risks.mitigation: repositories return unordered collections; the factory owns the whole rendered order, which is asserted in a unit test with real Vet and Specialty objects

risks.risk: A hard-coded string or a new bundle key missing from one locale fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which walks src/main and compares every bundle against messages.properties
risks.mitigation: reuse the existing keys where possible; any new key lands in messages.properties plus the nine translated bundles (messages_en.properties is intentionally empty and is skipped by the test)

risks.risk: Reading two repositories means two read-only transactions, so the page can observe a torn snapshot
risks.mitigation: accepted; NG-2 leaves the application with no write path for veterinarians or specialties, so no inconsistency is observable. Recorded in the ADR's Consequences

risks.risk: A record reached only from a template is invisible to GraalVM native-image analysis; SpEL property access may need a reflection hint
risks.mitigation: out of scope for the JVM build and its tests (@DisabledInNativeImage). If the native image is exercised, register the type in PetClinicRuntimeHints alongside the existing entries

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records; nothing to audit. Deviation from the prd-entry file_targets: the route goes in a new SpecialtyController rather than VetController, following the per-surface controller split the owner package already uses (OwnerController/PetController/VisitController) and the naming rule in architecture-principles.md § Naming; the template stays under templates/vets/ as the file target said. Test placement: the five derivation behaviors (grouping, multi-holding, exclusion of an unspecialized veterinarian, unheld specialty, stable order) are unit tests over real Vet and Specialty objects with no framework context; only the wiring, the view name, the as-stored rendering and the unlinked-navigation check need the web slice — testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid and § Mocking Policy. Seed data holds three specialties, all held, so edge cases 1 and 2 exist only in unit tests. Open product questions are not designed past: name order is chosen because it is deterministic and matches Vet.getSpecialties(), which does not settle the PRD's open question about which order is presented; a specialty held by nobody renders with an empty veterinarian list and no marker; no navigation entry is added. Vocabulary gap for product-requirements-expert: 'specialty directory' is PRD and test-name vocabulary but is absent from docs/ubiquitous-language.md; the type name SpecialtyDirectoryEntry adopts it. This agent does not write that file outside a foundational triage.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry is declared `public record`, but grep across the repository shows it is used only inside the `vet` package (SpecialtyController and the two test classes in the same package); no other package references it. This violates architecture-principles.md's Minimal Surface rule ("a type or member is module-internal unless another module uses it today") and breaks the visibility convention this same package already follows: SpecialtyController and VetController are both package-private. Widening SpecialtyDirectoryEntry to public makes an unused promise to future callers and is inconsistent with its sibling controller classes.
findings.fix: Drop the `public` modifier so `record SpecialtyDirectoryEntry(...)` is package-private, matching SpecialtyController/VetController. Verify Thymeleaf rendering (specialtyList.html) and the test classes (same package) still work after the change — they should, since all use sites are in-package.

approved_aspects: Cache hazard avoided correctly: directoryOf/holdersOf never mutate the veterinarians collection in place — they operate via Stream.sorted()/toList(), which return new lists, so the @Cacheable("vets") instance from VetRepository.findAll() is left untouched; SpecialtyDirectoryEntryTests.theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldLeaveTheCollectionsItReadsUntouched exercises this explicitly.

Stored-identity matching rule implemented exactly as specified: holds() uses !held.isNew() && held.getId().equals(specialty.getId()), correctly avoiding reliance on BaseEntity's absent equals/hashCode.
Record is a proper immutable value object: compact constructor null-checks specialtyName and defensively copies veterinarians via List.copyOf.
SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyController match established package conventions (public repository interface, package-private controller, constructor injection, single @GetMapping).
Javadoc on directoryOf explicitly documents the cache-aliasing hazard and why in-place mutation must be avoided, which is exactly the kind of context a future reader needs.
./gradlew checkFormat passes (task is named checkFormat, not checkJavaFormat, in this project's Gradle setup).
Message keys used in specialtyList.html (specialties, name, vets) exist in messages.properties and are localized in all locale variants.

Design matches the superseding ADR (2026-08-24-read-model-derivation-in-value-types.md) and system-design.md Contracts table: derivation and ordering live solely in the value type, controller only reads repositories and delegates.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every user-derived value through th:text only (entry.specialtyName, veterinarian.firstName/lastName). No th:utext, no th:inline, no th:href/th:src carrying stored data, no javascript: sink. Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping applies, and the application does not disable it. Class sweep across the changed templates and the whole vet package found no unescaped-output instance, so a stored specialty or vet name containing markup renders inert.

Injection exposure: SpecialtyRepository is a Spring Data derived-query interface (Repository<Specialty,Integer> with a bare findAll()); no JPQL string, no native query, no concatenation, no user-supplied fragment. SpecialtyController takes no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, or form binding, so there is no attacker-controlled value on the path to the data store. This matches the system-design threat-model row for SQL injection.

Transaction scoping: findAll() is annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true), matching VetRepository. The endpoint performs no write, and GET /specialties.html is side-effect-free, so the absence of CSRF protection (a documented application-wide posture) has no bearing on this route.

Endpoint exposure: the new route is unauthenticated, which is the application's documented pre-existing posture (docs/system-design.md Security Context: no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere in the codebase). The route adds attack surface but no new privilege boundary: it is read-only, parameterless, and reachable only by GET. docs/system-design.md Security Context was updated with the endpoint-exposure sentence, so the widened surface is recorded rather than silent.

Data exposure: the page publishes exactly specialty names and veterinarian first/last names. Both classes are already published unauthenticated by GET /vets.html and its serialized-collection sibling. SpecialtyDirectoryEntry projects only specialtyName plus the Vet list, and the template reads only firstName and lastName off each Vet, so no identifier, no telephone, no owner or pet data, and no internal field reaches the response. The one genuinely new datum is the existence of a specialty nobody holds, which is clinic-published reference data, not PII. No new class of data crosses the boundary.

Cache integrity: directoryOf receives the @Cacheable("vets") collection from VetRepository.findAll() and never mutates it - ordering is done with stream().sorted() into fresh lists, and the record's compact constructor takes List.copyOf. A caller cannot poison the shared vet cache through this path.

Availability: the no-pagination decision renders every specialty and its holders in one response. The data is bounded clinic reference data with no attacker-controlled growth path (specialties are seeded, and vet/specialty creation has no HTTP route), and the response carries two short strings per row. Not a practical resource-exhaustion vector; recorded as assessed, not raised as a finding.
Secrets: no credential, token, key, or password literal in the diff; no new logging statement, so no user-derived or sensitive value reaches a log sink.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set - no dependency added, removed, or version-bumped, so this slice introduces no new CVE surface. Spring Boot 4.1.0 and the Thymeleaf/Spring Data versions it manages are unchanged from the reviewed baseline.
Test surface: SpecialtyControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest with a @TestConfiguration supplying in-memory repository doubles; it disables no security machinery and carries no credential fixture.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The fail-closed guard in SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.holds() — `!held.isNew() && held.getId().equals(specialty.getId())` (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java:76) — has its `isNew()==true` short-circuit branch never exercised. JaCoCo confirms: 'L76 ... 1 of 4 branches missed.' Every Specialty built by the test factories (aSpecialtyNamed) is given an id, so no test ever adds an unsaved (no-id) Specialty to a Vet's held set. This branch is not incidental: the superseding design-block (line 8) names it as a deliberate, load-bearing behavior — 'the !isNew() guard fails closed rather than throwing... a directory derived over unsaved objects would silently render every specialty as unheld' — and states the constraint in terms of the tests setting ids, but the guard's actual effect (an unsaved specialty never matches) is left unverified. Line coverage reads 100% for the class, which is why this gap is invisible without a branch-level check.
findings.fix: Add a unit test (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotMatchAnUnsavedSpecialtyToAStoredOne) that builds a Vet holding a Specialty with the same name as a stored Specialty but with no id set (a bare `new Specialty()` with only the name set, not run through aSpecialtyNamed), calls directoryOf, and asserts the veterinarian does not appear under that stored specialty's entry — proving the fail-closed guard rather than just disciplining test data to avoid tripping it.

approved_aspects: All 8 PRD-driven behaviors (every specialty on one page, first-then-last vet naming, multi-specialty holding, unspecialized-vet omission, unheld specialty listed with no marker, empty-directory render, stable ordering including last-name-tie-break by first name then id, untranslated stored names) have dedicated unit and/or web-slice tests, all passing (14/14 green, 100% line coverage on SpecialtyDirectoryEntry and SpecialtyController)

Pyramid placement matches the brief's rationale: the five pure derivation behaviors are unit-tested over real Vet/Specialty objects with no framework context; only wiring, view name, as-stored rendering, and the unlinked-navigation check use @WebMvcTest, and no rule duplicates across layers

Mocking policy fully honored: no Mockito/mock-framework import in either test file; SpecialtyControllerTests uses hand-written @TestConfiguration doubles (a lambda SpecialtyRepository, an anonymous VetRepository) plus MockMvc as the one sanctioned boundary mock

BDD naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) used consistently across all 14 test methods; three-tier data naming honored — DENTISTRY/RADIOLOGY/SURGERY and HELD_SPECIALTY/UNHELD_SPECIALTY are role-named Tier-1 constants, no bare mystery literals, ids generated via a counter or explicit factory args

The cache-guard test (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldLeaveTheCollectionsItReadsUntouched) is genuine, not decorative: it passes real mutable ArrayLists (mimicking the @Cacheable vets collection) rather than List.of(), so an in-place-sort regression would actually flip this test red; verified against the current stream().sorted() implementation, which never mutates its input

The Specialty-id constraint from the design-block is honored: aSpecialtyNamed and aVeterinarianNumbered both assign ids before use, so every held-specialty match in the existing suite exercises the !isNew()==false path correctly

Construction wrapped in factory methods (aSpecialtyNamed, aVeterinarianNamed/aVeterinarianNumbered, anEntryFor) in both files; whole-object comparison via containsExactly(anEntryFor(...)) rather than field-picking assertions
AssertJ used throughout with no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue; collection-aware assertions (containsExactly, containsExactlyInAnyOrder, flatExtracting, isEmpty) used appropriately

approved_aspects: Round-2 verdict: APPROVED. The fix delta (docs/prd.md, docs/ubiquitous-language.md, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java, SpecialtyDirectoryEntryTests.java against prev_tree_sha 6b0618a) introduces no new security exposure, and every round-1 approved aspect still holds: SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, and templates/vets/specialtyList.html are byte-identical to the surface I approved at line 17, so the output-escaping, injection, endpoint-exposure, and data-exposure findings need no re-derivation.

Visibility narrowing (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java:33, public dropped): strictly reduces reachable API surface. The type is a read-model carrier with no security-relevant behavior, and narrowing it cannot widen any trust boundary. Only in-package callers exist (SpecialtyController plus the two same-package test classes), so no reflective or cross-package consumer is broken open. Least privilege applied, not weakened.

Fail-closed guard, now verified behaviorally (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java:76, `!held.isNew() && held.getId().equals(specialty.getId())`): identity matching is the safe outcome and the new test proves it. An unsaved held Specialty carrying the same NAME as a stored one does not match, so a name string can never cause a veterinarian to be published under a specialty they do not hold - the failure mode would have been an authorization-shaped over-disclosure (wrong association rendered as clinic fact), and the guard closes it. The short-circuit also keeps a null id off the `.equals` receiver, so no NullPointerException escapes into the request path; the inverse case (a stored specialty with a null id) is safe too, since `held.getId().equals(null)` returns false rather than throwing. Fail-closed on both axes: no spurious match, no 500.

New test surface (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotMatchAnUnsavedSpecialtyToAStoredOne, anUnsavedSpecialtyNamed): pure in-memory construction of real domain objects; no mock framework, no credential fixture, no security machinery disabled, no I/O, no network. It adds coverage of a security-relevant branch without adding attack surface.

Secret sweep over the delta: grep for password|secret|token|api key|credential across all added lines returns no hits. No new logging statement, so no user-derived or sensitive value reaches a log sink.

Supply chain: build.gradle, gradle/, and every dependency declaration are absent from the fix delta, so no dependency was added, removed, or version-bumped since round 1. The CVE surface is unchanged from the baseline I cleared at line 17; Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Thymeleaf/Spring Data versions still stand.

Documentation-only changes (prd.md narrative rephrased to drop the literal route, ubiquitous-language.md 'Specialty directory' entry, prd.md Design/ADR link line) carry no executable content and no security claim. Removing the literal path from PRD prose is not security-by-obscurity being relied on - docs/system-design.md still records the route and its unauthenticated exposure explicitly, so the documented threat model stays accurate.

Class sweep across the whole delta for the classes I reason about (unescaped output, injection sink, secret literal, authz-shaped matching logic, dependency change) found no further instance beyond those assessed above.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Additive and contained: all four production files are new and sit in the vet package, no existing production file is modified at all (the only edited files are docs), and there is no schema, dependency, configuration, cache, or navigation change. The single new surface is one GET route, /specialties.html, and no sensitive path is touched.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk and the template. The derivation matches by persisted identity with a fail-closed guard (!held.isNew() && held.getId().equals(specialty.getId())), so an unsaved specialty of the same name cannot match a stored one; specialty order is by stored name and holder order is last name, first name, id-nulls-last; both input collections are read through stream copies so the cached VetRepository list is never reordered. Comparator null-intolerance on names mirrors the pre-existing Vet.getSpecialties(), and the EAGER @ManyToMany rules out a lazy-initialization failure the web slice could not see. The only wrinkle is cost, not behavior: getSpecialties() is re-sorted and copied once per specialty-vet pair, irrelevant at clinic scale.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert outcomes, not the implementation. Nine unit tests over real Vet and Specialty objects pin the boundaries the code actually decides: an unheld specialty is present with an empty holder list, a vet holding nothing is absent, an unsaved specialty does not match a stored one, ties break by first name then id, and both source collections are unchanged afterwards. Six web-slice tests render the real Thymeleaf template and assert on produced HTML with negative assertions (no paging parameter, no reversed name order, no navigation link). No end-to-end request hits the route against the real database, but PetClinicIntegrationTests boots the full context, so the new SpecialtyRepository bean wiring is proven to resolve.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round 2 is a clean unanimous approval: all four reviewers the plan dispatched approved with empty findings arrays, no escalate tag and no bar_clause anywhere. The round-1 findings (public visibility on a package-internal record, a missing ubiquitous-language entry, an embedded literal route in the PRD, an unexercised isNew() branch) were each fixed and named as resolved by the reviewer that raised them.

scope_deviation.note: Zero consultations and zero build retries against the current design block, and the diff matches the requirement's stated surface with nothing extra. The one design revision was bookkeeping, not a scope fight: the autofix audit flagged the ADR index row as uncovered by the design block's file list. The PRD supersede was the doc reviewer's wording fix, and the three new open questions are honest disclosure of what the slice deliberately left undecided.

rationale: Purely additive read-only page, entirely inside the vet package, with no existing production file touched. The derivation logic reads correctly at every boundary and the tests pin those boundaries with real objects. Confirm and merge; no hunk needs a second look.
